div.head: EGu 5.1
div.ab: ⁊ ealle Godes gerihto forðige man georne be Godes mildse ⁊ be þam wítan þe witan toledan.
⁊ ealle Godes gerihte fyrðrie man geórne be Godes mildse ⁊ be ðam wítan ðe witán toledan.
Et omnes Dei rectitudines pacificentur sedulo per Dei misericordiam et per witam, quam sapientes edicent (addicent).
⁊ ealle Godes gerihto forðige man georne be Godes mildse ⁊ be þam wítan þe witan toledan
And ealle Godes gerihto forðige man georne be Godes mildse and be þam witan þe witan toledan.
Und alle Kirchen-Gerechtsame fördere man eifrig wegen Gottes Gnade und wegen der Strafen, welche die Witan darauf setzten.
And let all the Church’s dues be zealously furthered for the sake of God’s mercy and for the sake of the fines which the councillors laid down for them.
And all ecclesiastical dues shall be promptly rendered, on pain of forfeiting God's mercy and incurring the fines which the councillors have imposed.
And all God’s dues shall be rendered assiduously for God’s mercy and because of the penalties which the councilors assigned.

Die Benutzer V Atr 12, 2 = VI 21, 1 = VIII 14 = I Cn 14 haben fyrðrie, das also bereits im 10. Jh. im Text stand wie in B Ld. Dass es archetyp war, beweist Q: seine Vorlage las friðie, eine häufige Verderbnis aus fyrðrie; s. Wb: friðian

Those who used it, V Atr 12, 2 = VI 21, 1 = VIII 14 = I Cn 14, have fyrðrie, which therefore already stood in the text in the 10th cent., as in B Ld. That it belonged to the archetype is proved by Q: his exemplar read friðie, a frequent corruption of fyrðrie; see Wb: friðian
Statt Strafen sagen Benutzer homiletisch ‘wie es nötig ist’. — Zu ‘Gottes Gnade’ vgl. AGu Pro⁹
Instead of ‘punish’ those who used it say, homiletically, ‘as is necessary’. — On ‘God’s grace’ cf. AGu Pro⁹
Vgl. Einl. 19
Cf. Introduction 19
